newsitem.title: USA: White House sets up global climate plan task force.
newsitem.headline: White House sets up global climate plan task force.

text.p: The White House is setting up a task force to coordinate and secure support for the Clinton administration's proposals in global climate negotiations, Assistant Secretary of Energy Dirk Forrester said Wednesday.
Forrester was chosen to chair the interagency task force and was set to begin work at the White House next week.

The group's main role will be to "improve communications" with and get input from business and environmental groups, unions, state and local communities, and Congress, he told reporters after speaking at an Aluminum Association meeting.
The administration is involved in international talks set to culminate in December in Kyoto, Japan, with an agreement to curb greenhouse gas emissions after 2000.

Last year, the United States said it would support binding targets for emissions cuts. But the administration wanted each country to be able to set its own policies to meet emissions budgets and wanted deadlines to come into force beginning in 2010, rather than earlier.
"The United States has been vey forceful in saying our interest in binding (targets) is in the medium term, not the short term," Forrester told the Aluminum Association.
Washington was also pushing a plan that would make countries meet targets within "packages of years" instead of in single years.
"If you focus too much on single years, there can be lots of ups and downs that can be associated with weather, (and) with business cycles," Forrester said.
The administration last month laid out a proposal that would set emissions caps for industrialized countries and let countries bank and trade emissions allowances.
Forrester said the administration would be working "over the next nine months and probably on into next year" on a set of proposals to carry out the final international agreement.
But he said it was not yet clear whether the administration would submit a set of recommendations to Congress for complying with the agreement when it is sent to the Senate for approval.
